subject: Proof of Claim & Evidence Deadlines — MSA Indemnity
messages:
From: Carla Mendez <carla@brightfarm.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightFarm Legal <legal@brightfarm.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: IP claim notice window and evidence we can provide

Hi Sean,

Following up from our procurement call — BrightFarm's legal team needs to understand the deadlines we have to comply with a third-party IP claim notice under the MSA. Two quick asks: 1) What notice timing/proof-of-claim windows does Redwood expect for an "infringement" claim, and 2) what specific technical evidence (logs, model snapshots, prompt history) will Redwood need to defend?

We're trying to line up internal owners and see whether this will touch our infra team (they want lead time). If you can send a proposed timeline and a short evidence checklist we can include with the SOW, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Carla
Legal Ops | BrightFarm
[Attachment: intake-questions.pdf (stub)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Carla Mendez <carla@brightfarm.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IP claim notice window and evidence we can provide

Carla —

Short answer up front: Redwood requires prompt written notice of a claim plus access to (a) the allegedly infringing inputs/outputs and (b) operational artifacts sufficient to replicate the request (request ID/logs, model version, sequence length, and any cached prefixes). For timing, our standard is: notice within 30 days of customer becoming aware; preservation of live logs for 60 days; formal evidence handover (packaged) within 14 days of notice where possible.

I want Legal to weigh in on the exact drafting and any insurance interplay — looping in Kimberly and Karthik. Attached is a draft evidence checklist we use internally that we can adapt for BrightFarm.

Next steps: Kimberly to confirm the proposed timeline and any alternative language if the customer requests longer preservation. Karthik — please advise on whether 60 days of logs is realistic for typical BrightFarm telemetry volumes (cc'ing infra).

Cheers,
Sean
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evidence-list-template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Carla Mendez <carla@brightfarm.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IP claim notice window and evidence we can provide

Carla/Sean —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few legal points and a proposed concession that might be acceptable to both parties:

- Notice timing: Redwood is comfortable with a 30-day notice-from-awareness standard. We will accept a written notice delivered by email to security-incident@redwood.com.
- Evidence preservation: Redwood can commit to preserving live request/response logs for 90 days if BrightFarm executes a narrow data access addendum (we need the right to store a copy of the minimal relevant logs for defense). Without the addendum, we can preserve for 60 days and provide the BrightFarm team with a downloadable package.
- Defense control: Redwood prefers to retain the right to control defense for third-party IP claims but will agree to reasonably cooperate and allow customer input where the customer's confidential information is at stake — propose a 30-day lead for customer to nominate counsel.
- Insurance/offload: If customer provides an insurance carrier that will step in, we can coordinate direct contact; add clause that carrier must accept Redwood's chosen outside counsel or we reserve approval rights.

I've attached a redline of the MSA indemnity paragraph with language toggles (preserve 60 v 90 days, defense control mechanics, and a narrow evidence-supply clause). Also included an "evidence package checklist" (the spreadsheet Sean attached).

Proposed ask to BrightFarm: confirm whether their procurement team can sign the data access addendum; if not, confirm they accept 60 days and the downloadable package approach.

-Kimberly
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: msa-redline_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Carla Mendez <carla@brightfarm.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IP claim notice window and evidence we can provide

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick internal check: our procurement lead says they cannot sign an addendum that permits Redwood to retain copies of our logs; they're only willing to accept a packaged export and a 60-day preservation window. They will however agree to a 30-day notice and the defense-control language you proposed if we can: (a) require Redwood to provide a redacted defense summary to BrightFarm within 45 days of taking control, and (b) commit to escalation to mediation if counsel teams disagree on a settlement that would materially impact BrightFarm.

If those two concessions are acceptable, we can move forward and Karthik, we'll need your ops assessment on whether 60-day preservation + packaging is low lift.

Thanks —
Carla

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Carla Mendez <carla@brightfarm.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IP claim notice window and evidence we can provide

Team —

Ops note: 60-day preservation + packaged export is feasible. We'll need to add an automated export job scoped to the request IDs in the notice (we can avoid long-term retention in our primary store by writing the package to a short-lived bucket and delivering the link). Estimate: 2-3 days of engineering work to parameterize the job and test, then 1 day to run the first production export. No infra changes required; slightly elevated SRE attention during the first run.

If BrightFarm confirms the 60-day route, Kimberly: recommend we accept their redaction/mediation asks with the addition of limited carveouts for privileged Redwood communications. Sean — I'll prepare an ops note and a short runbook for the export flow once legal flags final language.

-Karthik
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
